variants.headline: Looking back: home-world ship reaches the colony
variants.sub: The colony has received the arrival of a home-world ship.
variants.body:
We return to {first_reported}. Our report recorded this: A ship from the home world had arrived in the colony.

The gazette records the arrival without presuming the contents of the vessel. A notice of a ship reaching the colony should not be enlarged into an account of deliveries or administrative arrangements not supplied here. The event has sufficient public significance without adding particulars to its official description.

The event remains part of the record. Whether subsequent developments met the standard it raised is a separate question, not something the old headline can answer by itself.

We welcome {target} in this assessment. A tangible connection with the home world deserves recognition, while a fair account can acknowledge the arrival without pretending that every need has thereby been satisfied.

variants.headline: Looking back: an arrival on the colonial route
variants.sub: A vessel from the home world has reached {colony}.
variants.body:
Looking back to {first_reported}, this was the news: The colony had received the arrival of a home-world ship.

The gazette records the arrival without presuming the contents of the vessel. A notice of a ship reaching the colony should not be enlarged into an account of deliveries or administrative arrangements not supplied here. The event has sufficient public significance without adding particulars to its official description.

Time changes the distance from an event, not the need to judge it carefully. Any claim about improvement or deterioration needs more than a recollection of the original news.

We welcome {target} in this assessment. A tangible connection with the home world deserves recognition, while a fair account can acknowledge the arrival without pretending that every need has thereby been satisfied.

variants.headline: Looking back: the distant connection comes into port
variants.sub: A ship from the home world has arrived in the colony.
variants.body:
The headline belongs to {first_reported}. Our original account recorded this: A vessel from the home world had reached {colony}.

The gazette records the arrival without presuming the contents of the vessel. A notice of a ship reaching the colony should not be enlarged into an account of deliveries or administrative arrangements not supplied here. The event has sufficient public significance without adding particulars to its official description.

What has changed since then should be examined against that original record. What has not changed is the need to distinguish an established event from the hopes or fears attached to it.

We welcome {target} in this assessment. A tangible connection with the home world deserves recognition, while a fair account can acknowledge the arrival without pretending that every need has thereby been satisfied.
